front: Procedure: box fill count (what counts as 1, 2, 0)
back:
Each conductor entering and spliced/terminated = 1; unbroken pass-through = 1; a loop ≥ 2 × the 300.14 free length = 2
Pigtails that never leave the box = 0
Internal cable clamps = 1 (largest conductor present), each support fitting (stud/hickey) = 1
Each device yoke = 2 (largest conductor on that yoke)
All EGCs together = 1 (largest EGC); 2020 adds ¼ allowance for each EGC beyond four
Multiply counts by Table 314.16(B)(1) volumes: 14 AWG 2.00 · 12 AWG 2.25 · 10 AWG 2.50 · 8 AWG 3.00 · 6 AWG 5.00 in³
note: Verify the 2020 wording in 314.16(B)(5) for the 'more than four EGCs' quarter-allowance; the rest is settled.

front: Worked: box for two 12-2 NM cables (with EGC) feeding one duplex receptacle, internal clamps
back:
Conductors: 4 × 12 AWG = 4
EGCs (all) = 1
Clamps = 1
Device yoke = 2
Total 8 × 2.25 in³ = 18.0 in³ → a 4 × 1½ square (21 in³) or a 3 × 2 × 3½ device box (18 in³) works; a 3 × 2 × 2½ (12.5 in³) does not

front: Procedure: conduit fill for mixed conductor sizes
back:
1. Table 5: area of each conductor (THHN: 12 AWG 0.0133 · 10 AWG 0.0211 · 8 AWG 0.0366 · 6 AWG 0.0507 · 4 AWG 0.0824 · 3 AWG 0.0973 · 2 AWG 0.1158 · 1 AWG 0.1562 in²)
2. Sum them
3. Table 4: column for the raceway type at 40 % (>2 wires), 31 % (2), 53 % (1); nipple ≤ 24 in → 60 % (Note 4)
4. Pick the first trade size whose allowed area ≥ the sum
Same-size wires only: Annex C is faster

front: Worked: EMT for 3 × 6 AWG THHN + 1 × 8 AWG THHN + 1 × 10 AWG THHN EGC
back:
3 × 0.0507 = 0.1521
+ 0.0366 + 0.0211 = 0.2098 in²
EMT at 40 % (Table 4): ¾ in = 0.213 ✔ · ½ in = 0.122 ✗
→ ¾ in EMT (tight; 1 in = 0.346 gives pulling room)

front: Worked: how many 12 AWG THHN in 1 in EMT (40 % = 0.346 in²)?
back:
0.346 ÷ 0.0133 = 26.0 → 26 conductors
Note 7: when the result's decimal is 0.8 or higher, round up (e.g., 15.8 → 16); below 0.8, round down
Annex C Table C.1 lists the same answer for same-size conductors

front: Procedure: ampacity with temperature + bundling corrections (worked: 8 × 10 AWG THHN in one conduit at 45 °C)
back:
1. Start at the conductor's insulation column: 10 AWG THHN 90 °C = 40 A
2. × temperature factor (Table 310.15(B)(1)(1), 90 °C column, 41–45 °C) 0.87 → 34.8 A
3. × adjustment (Table 310.15(C)(1), 7–9 conductors) 0.70 → 24.4 A
4. Final ampacity is the lesser of that and the termination column (110.14(C): 10 AWG → 60 °C = 30 A for ≤ 100 A circuits unless listed for 75 °C) → 24.4 A governs
5. 240.4(D) cap 30 A still applies to the OCPD

front: Worked: how many current-carrying conductors — 2 MWBCs (3-wire from a 120/240 V 1φ panel) + 1 × 120 V 2-wire circuit in one EMT?
back:
MWBC on 1φ 3-wire: neutral carries only the unbalance → not counted (310.15(E)(1)) → 2 each = 4
2-wire circuit: hot + neutral both count = 2
EGCs never count (310.15(F))
Total 6 → 80 % adjustment
On a 3φ 4-wire wye with ≥ 50 % nonlinear load, the neutral counts (310.15(E)(3))

front: Worked: THWN conductors in EMT lying directly on a rooftop (½ in above the roof) at 38 °C ambient
back:
2020 rooftop rule: raceways or cables less than ⅞ in above the roof add 33 °C (60 °F) → 38 + 33 = 71 °C design ambient
THWN is 75 °C insulation; Table 310.15(B)(1)(1) gives no 75 °C factor above 70 °C → the conductor can't be used there
Fix: raise the raceway ≥ ⅞ in above the roof (no adder), or use 90 °C conductors (THWN-2: 0.50 at 71–75 °C)
Exception: XHHW-2 is exempt from the adder

front: Temperature correction factors worth memorizing (75 °C and 90 °C columns)
Worked: smallest Cu conductor for a 150 A noncontinuous feeder, 75 °C terminations, no derating; same for aluminum
back:
Table 310.16, 75 °C column: 1/0 Cu = 150 A ✔
Al 75 °C: 3/0 Al = 155 A ✔ (2/0 Al = 135 A ✗)
Rule of thumb: Al runs about two sizes larger than Cu for the same ampacity

1/0 AWG and larger only (limited exceptions)
Each set: same length, material, size (CM), insulation type, terminated the same way
Each raceway or cable gets a full set, including an EGC sized per 250.122 for the OCPD
Ampacity = sum of the sets, then apply the adjustment factor for the conductor count in each raceway

front: Worked burial depths: UF cable for a 20 A 120 V GFCI-protected circuit to a lamp post; PVC under a residential driveway; RMC in a yard
back:
UF, 120 V ≤ 20 A with GFCI: 12 in (Table 300.5 column 4)
PVC under one-/two-family dwelling driveway: 18 in (column 3)
RMC/IMC: 6 in (column 2)
Direct-burial cable default: 24 in; under a 4 in concrete slab: 18 in

front: Worked: NM cable through bored holes in studs — hole edge 1 in from the stud face. OK?
back:
No: the hole edge must be ≥ 1¼ in from the nearest edge of the framing member, else a 1/16 in steel plate is required (300.4(A)(1))
Same 1¼ in for cables run parallel to framing (300.4(D))
Rigid metal, IMC, EMT and RMC don't need the plate

front: Support intervals — worked quiz: EMT, RMC ¾ in, NM, MC
back:
EMT: within 3 ft of each box, then ≤ 10 ft (358.30)
RMC: within 3 ft of boxes, then Table 344.30(B)(2): ½–¾ in 10 ft · 1 in 12 ft · 1¼–1½ in 14 ft · 2–2½ in 16 ft · 3 in and larger 20 ft
NM: within 12 in of boxes, then ≤ 4½ ft (334.30)
MC: within 12 in of terminations, then ≤ 6 ft (330.30)

front: Worked: pull box for a straight pull of 3 in conduit; angle pull with one 3 in and one 2 in in the same wall
back:
Straight: length ≥ 8 × largest raceway = 24 in (314.28(A)(1))
Angle/U pull: distance to opposite wall ≥ 6 × largest + sum of the others in that row = 18 + 2 = 20 in (314.28(A)(2))
Between raceways with the same conductor: ≥ 6 × largest = 18 in
Applies to 4 AWG and larger conductors

front: Underground run details that get asked
back:
Direct-buried cables/conduits emerging from grade: protected up to 8 ft above grade (300.5(D)(1))
All conductors of a circuit in the same trench/raceway (300.5(I))
Backfill: no rocks/sharp material against cables; sand or protection where needed (300.5(F))
Warning tape on underground service conductors not in raceway, ≥ 12 in above (300.5(D)(3))
